question.text: A key disadvantage of the LLP form for Indian AIFs compared to the trust form is:

answer.text: LLPs cannot be SEBI-registered as AIFs.
Investor details are published on the MCA website, losing the confidentiality available in a trust structure.
LLPs attract mandatory 5% stamp duty on each capital call.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** All LLP partners - including investor-partners - are disclosed on the MCA portal. This is the opposite of the trust structure where beneficiary details remain confidential. Many HNIs and family offices prefer the trust for this reason. **The Trap:** LLPs DO offer limited liability (defining feature). SEBI DOES register LLPs. Stamp duty claim is fabricated. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C contrasts LLP vs trust. XIX-A rarely tests this nuance. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If an LP insists on an LLP for tax reasons (transparency), at least run a parallel trust-form scheme so other LPs can preserve confidentiality.
